parameters.content:
## 0) Check the ticket is not already solved or closed

Runs first, and on purpose does NOT post an internal note or reopen the ticket.

Why the guard: on 2026-07-23 Zendesk redelivered a ticket-created webhook 8h37m late. The automation re-ran on the original first email, found the refundable charges already consumed, and emailed the customer a refund rejection after having already granted the refund.

Why no internal note here: the shared Do not proceed path sets the ticket back to open. On a solved ticket that would re-queue it for agents and could re-fire the 2nd-message trigger.
## 1) Check for blocked emails

## 2) One active ticket per requester

Active = new, open, pending, hold. Solved and closed do NOT block - a returning customer with only resolved history is eligible for automation.

Custom statuses (e.g. In Progress) report under their base status, so no config column is needed.

**Keeper** = oldest active ticket (created_at asc). It proceeds.
**Loser** = any other active ticket. It merges itself into the keeper and returns false, silently.

Only the loser acts on itself - the keeper never touches its siblings. That removes the race where two concurrent executions close each other.
## 3) Check for contact form cancellations

# Do not proceed (loud)
Blocked email / user not found / contact form cancellation / dedup disabled.
Internal note + set to open + manual handling.

# Proceed
All checks passed. Wire the main automation after this node.

# Do not proceed (silent)
This ticket is a duplicate. No note, no status change - the handler merges it into the keeper, which closes it.

Return shape is identical (proceedWithAutomation: false), so the calling workflow needs no change.

parameters.content:
## 1b) Auto-solve emails

Same matching logic as the blocklist (substring, case-insensitive, `active` respected), against **cs_email_autosolve**.

On a match the ticket is solved immediately with a private internal note and **no public comment**, so the customer is never notified. Tagged `autosolve_email`, and the category is set to **Duplicate contact** (`category_value_duplicate_contact`).

The category is set because 14 of 16 brands have that field marked `required: true` - solving without it can be rejected by Zendesk outright.

Runs AFTER the blocklist on purpose: if an address ends up on both lists, blocklist wins and a human looks at it.

The table is global and starts empty, so this branch is inert until a row is added - no per-brand config flag needed.

nodes.name: Spam check enabled?
nodes.notes: Gated on cs_project_config.spam_check_enabled AND spam_model_id being set. Either missing = skip the AI call entirely.

nodes.name: AI: Spam check
nodes.notes: onError is continueRegularOutput so an API failure falls through to not-spam.

nodes.name: Parse spam verdict
nodes.notes: Fail-open: any error, missing content, unparseable JSON or sub-threshold confidence results in solve_as_spam false.

nodes.name: Is spam?
nodes.notes: True only when the model said spam AND confidence cleared the configured threshold AND the call did not fail.

nodes.name: Zendesk: Solve as spam
nodes.notes: Private note + status solved + tag spam_auto_solved, and the Spam category value when configured. additional_tags is used so existing tags are not clobbered.

nodes.name: Do not proceed (spam)
nodes.notes: Same return shape as every other terminal - the calling workflow needs no change.

parameters.content:
## 1c) AI spam check

Last of the three pre-flight gates, on purpose: the blocklist and auto-solve tables are deterministic and free, so they get first refusal. As patterns emerge, addresses move onto those lists and this node matters less.

Runs before the requester lookup and dedup, so spam never reaches the payments service, never triggers a merge, and never costs a Zendesk user search.

**Gated by** `spam_check_enabled` + `spam_model_id`. Threshold from `spam_confidence_threshold` (falls back to 0.97).

**Fail-open everywhere.** API error, timeout, empty or unparseable response, missing confidence, or confidence below threshold all result in the ticket proceeding normally. `spam_check_failed` is set explicitly in the output because `onError: continueRegularOutput` hides these runs from error-status execution searches.

On a match: solved, private note, tag `spam_auto_solved`, and the Spam & Marketing category value when `category_value_spam_marketing` is populated.

nodes.name: Build auto-solve payload
nodes.notes: Builds the PUT body natively so the category field can be set alongside status. Skips the category field if either the field id or the per-brand value is unconfigured.

nodes.name: High risk check enabled?
nodes.notes: cs_project_config.high_risk_check_enabled. Empty or false = OFF (opt-in), same convention as spam_check_enabled and dedupe_merge_enabled.

nodes.name: Get High Risk Keywords
nodes.notes: cs_high_risk_keywords. GLOBAL - no project_key column. The same phrase list applies to every brand; only the check itself is per-project.

nodes.name: Build high risk payload
nodes.notes: Builds the PUT natively so the tag, note, status and allow-automation field go in one request. In monitoring mode only the tag and note are sent - no status change, no allow_automation change, and the ticket continues into automation.

nodes.name: High risk enforce?
nodes.notes: True = stop automation. False = monitoring mode, fall through to the spam gate and carry on as normal.

nodes.name: Do not proceed (high risk)
nodes.notes: Same return shape as every other terminal - the calling workflow needs no change. The note and status were already written by Zendesk: Flag high risk, so this does NOT route through the shared loud-fail path.

parameters.content:
## 1d) High-risk keyword check

Runs after the blocklist and auto-solve tables, and **before the spam gate and the dedupe merge** - both of those solve or close the ticket silently, and a legal threat or a self-harm mention must never disappear that way.

**Table:** `cs_high_risk_keywords`. Global, no `project_key` - one phrase list for every brand. Rows are switched on and off with `active`.

**Matching:** normalise both sides, then token-sequence match anchored with `(^| )needle( |$)`. A multi-word phrase must match as a consecutive run, so `several emails` never fires on `several` alone.

**Tier precedence C > A > B**, matching queue urgency (safety-review, Priority, Standard). A ticket matching several tiers takes the highest-risk one. Every match is listed in the note, not just the winner.

**Two independent switches in cs_project_config:**
- `high_risk_check_enabled` - master on/off, per project, opt-in
- `high_risk_enforce` - OFF = monitoring (tag + note only, bot still replies), ON = tag + note + status open + `allow_automation _no_` + automation stops

Start with enforce OFF to size the daily volume per tier before committing staff to the queues. Tier B profanity in particular could pull a large share of ordinary refund tickets out of automation.
